content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To shoot an arrow, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Retrieve the bow from the storage locker (2 minutes)
Step 2. Inspect the bow limbs for cracks or splinters (3 minutes)
Step 3. Check the target face for wear and tear (1 minute)
Step 4. Apply wax to the bowstring (5 minutes)
Step 5. Set up the ground quiver (2 minutes)
Step 6. Verify the stabilizer balance (4 minutes)
Step 7. Clear the shooting range of debris (10 minutes)
Step 8. Tighten the finger tab screws (1 minute)
Step 9. Adjust the arm guard straps (30 seconds)
Step 10. Install the dampeners on the limbs (5 minutes)
Step 11. Check the arrow rest alignment (4 minutes)
Step 12. Inspect the nocking point on the string (2 minutes)
Step 13. Select a matching set of arrows (5 minutes)
Step 14. Place the arrow on the rest (5 seconds)
Step 15. Clean the arrow shafts (10 minutes)
Step 16. Inspect the fletching on each arrow (3 minutes)
Step 17. Check the wind speed and direction (1 minute)
Step 18. Put on the chest guard (1 minute)
Step 19. Take a proper stance on the shooting line (15 seconds)
Step 20. Visualize the trajectory of the shot (30 seconds)
Step 21. Check the plunger tension (2 minutes)
Step 22. Hook the fingers onto the string (5 seconds)
Step 23. Check the clicker position (2 minutes)
Step 24. Adjust the sight for distance (1 minute)
Step 25. Select the primary arrow for the shot (10 seconds)
Step 26. Consult the archery manual for safety (20 minutes)
Step 27. Identify the specific target lane (10 seconds)
Step 28. Verify the nock tightness (1 minute)
Step 29. Raise the bow toward the target (5 seconds)
Step 30. Apply grip tape to the riser handle (10 minutes)
Step 31. Burnish the string wax with leather (2 minutes)
Step 32. Adjust the peep sight height (3 minutes)
Step 33. Square the shoulders (5 seconds)
Step 34. Check the bow sling tightness (1 minute)
Step 35. Calibrate the rangefinder (5 minutes)
Step 36. Clear the mind of distractions (2 minutes)
Step 37. Confirm the backstop is secure (5 minutes)
Step 38. Check the tiller measurements (6 minutes)
Step 39. Extend the bow arm fully (3 seconds)
Step 40. Draw the bowstring to the anchor point (3 seconds)
Step 41. Adjust the limb bolts for draw weight (8 minutes)
Step 42. Find the reference point on the chin (2 seconds)
Step 43. Align the string with the riser (5 seconds)
Step 44. Check the arrow spine rating (10 minutes)
Step 45. Breathe in deeply (3 seconds)
Step 46. Tighten the weight on the long rod (2 minutes)
Step 47. Unpack the toolkit (3 minutes)
Step 48. Check the draw length consistency (2 minutes)
Step 49. Measure the distance to the target (1 minute)
Step 50. Glue a loose vane back onto a shaft (15 minutes)
Step 51. String the bow using a bowstringing tool (2 minutes)
Step 52. Check the brace height (1 minute)
Step 53. Check the limb alignment (5 minutes)
Step 54. Wipe down the riser with a cloth (2 minutes)
Step 55. Put on the finger tab (30 seconds)
Step 56. Inspect the bowstring loops (1 minute)
Step 57. Set the sight pin to the zero mark (4 minutes)
Step 58. Check the tension in the back muscles (5 seconds)
Step 59. Tighten the side rod bushings (3 minutes)
Step 60. Snap the nock onto the string (2 seconds)
Step 61. Look through the sight aperture (3 seconds)
Step 62. Adjust the finger pressure on the string (2 seconds)
Step 63. Tighten the arrow tips (3 minutes)
Step 64. Perform a final safety scan of the field (1 minute)
Step 65. Squeeze the shoulder blades together (2 seconds)
Step 66. Focus the eyes on the gold center (5 seconds)
Step 67. Confirm no one is behind the target (10 seconds)
Step 68. Hold the breath (2 seconds)
Step 69. Clean the sight lens (2 minutes)
Step 70. Tighten the bow's mounting screws (4 minutes)
Step 71. Apply serving thread to a worn spot (10 minutes)
Step 72. Check the arrow points for sharpness (2 minutes)
Step 73. Put on the arm guard (1 minute)
Step 74. Check the clicker spring tension (2 minutes)
Step 75. Lubricate the arrow rest pivot (5 minutes)
Step 76. Double check the bow weight (3 minutes)
Step 77. Check the arrow clearance (5 minutes)
Step 78. Check the nock rotation (1 minute)
Step 79. Expand through the clicker (1 second)
Step 80. Verify the sight windage (2 minutes)
Step 81. Check the fletching glue dryness (10 minutes)
Step 82. Inspect the riser for cracks (5 minutes)
Step 83. Check the scope level bubble (1 minute)
Step 84. Clean the arrow rest (2 minutes)
Step 85. Check the bow's serial number (1 minute)
Step 86. Center the sight pin on the target (2 seconds)
Step 87. Engage the core muscles (3 seconds)
Step 88. Check the stabilizer vibration (2 minutes)
Step 89. Release the bowstring (0.1 seconds)
Step 90. Check the sight mounting bracket (2 minutes)
